chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubayda Al-Hadda', who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'A woman is not married (as an additional wife) upon her paternal aunt, nor upon her maternal aunt, except with the permission of the paternal aunt and the maternal aunt.'

key_terms.تُنْكَحُ: Is married (passive voice, referring to taking as a wife)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a woman if her aunt is already married to the same man?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the condition of 'ijma'' (consistency) in polygyny by requiring the consent of the existing aunt, distinguishing it from the general prohibition of marrying two sisters simultaneously. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the importance of familial harmony and the specific rights of co-wives within the extended family structure, as narrated through the chain of the Six Companions. It serves as a practical legal precedent for resolving potential conflicts between co-wives who share a close kinship bond.
